transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep forgetting everyday things—calls I promised to make, appointments I just wrote down, even simple errands—and it’s starting to cause problems with my husband’s care. I've always managed to get by, but with his health needs ramping up, I just feel like I'm constantly letting things slip through the cracks.
Have you noticed your memory problems getting steadily worse over time, or do they come and go with some days being much clearer than others?

It’s really hard to tell, honestly. Ever since I took on coordinating my husband's care a little over a year ago, the struggle has just felt fairly constant and overwhelming. I haven't really paid close attention to whether some days are clearer than others because I'm just trying to keep my head above water.
Do you ever have periods during the day where your thinking is noticeably more confused or foggy, followed by times when you feel much clearer?

No, I haven't really noticed my thinking fluctuating or going in and out of foggy and clear periods throughout the day like that. It feels much more constant, like a steady fog of being overwhelmed rather than something that comes and goes in waves.
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your ability to do familiar tasks, like managing bills or cooking, that used to feel routine?

Yes, absolutely. When I sit down to manage our bills and calendars, I just end up with piles of paper all over the dining table and get too overwhelmed to decide what to tackle first. Even cooking has become a struggle because if I'm trying to follow a recipe, the slightest thing distracts me and I completely lose my place.
Have you noticed any difficulty with recognizing familiar people or places, or becoming disoriented in environments you know well?
No, I haven't had any trouble with that at all. I still recognize everyone I know, and I don't get lost or disoriented in places I'm familiar with.
Have you ever been told that you seem confused, drowsy, or unusually irritable at times, even when you don't remember it yourself?

No, no one has ever told me that I seem drowsy, irritable, or confused in a way that I don't remember. I certainly get overwhelmed and forgetful, but I am always fully aware of it when it's happening.
Do you ever find yourself having trouble following conversations or staying focused for long periods, even if you're not distracted by something specific?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. When I'm on the phone, my mind will easily drift off to my own thoughts, and I'll suddenly realize I completely missed what the person just said. I also find myself avoiding tasks that require a lot of mental effort, like filling out insurance forms, because I lose track of what I'm doing so quickly.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for more than a couple of weeks at a time?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad, down, or hopeless. But I do feel very overwhelmed and stressed, and I'm constantly anxious about making a mistake with my husband's care.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent cognitive complaints involving memory, attention, and executive dysfunction in the context of significant psychosocial stress from caregiving responsibilities. There is no evidence of fluctuating cognition, impaired consciousness, disorientation, or depressive mood. Symptoms are better explained by adjustment disorder with cognitive symptoms under stress rather than major neurocognitive disorder or unipolar depression, though depressive features are absent. The diagnosis of F32.9 (Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified) was retained as per provided candidates, but clinical presentation suggests possible adjustment disorder with mixed disturbance of emotions and conduct (F43.2.3), which is not among listed candidates.
